sections.subtitle: A kernel slides across the image
sections.description:
A convolution applies a small kernel to every local patch of an image. The kernel learns to detect edges, textures, or other patterns.

Weight sharing is the key: the same kernel is reused across the whole image.

sections.subtitle: Pooling and channels
sections.description:
Channels let a layer learn multiple feature maps. Pooling reduces spatial size and makes the representation more robust to small shifts.

Modern vision models often use strided convolutions instead of explicit pooling, but the idea is the same: compress space while keeping useful signal.
